alerts_held.detail: 11.24% of net liquidation ($6,751 of $60,068.80), over the 10% single-position ceiling and under the 12% mandatory-review level.
alerts_held.reason: SPWO is the SP Funds S&P World ex-US ETF - a diversified Shariah-compliant benchmark ETF, the same instrument class as SPUS. The concentration-exclusion rule in st0ck_rules.md states its rationale ('not a single-stock concentration risk') but names only SPUS, so it does not literally cover SPWO. Firing a single-position concentration alert on a broad index ETF looked like exactly the false positive that exclusion was written to suppress, so no email was sent. Awaiting a decision on whether to extend the exclusion to SPWO.
alerts_held.unblocks: If the user says SPWO is NOT excluded, this becomes a live breach and should alert on the next run.

notes: last_snapshot.json and today_alerts.json did not exist in the repo before this run; both were created here. No prior baseline was available for snapshot-to-snapshot comparison, so intraday moves were taken from IBKR daily P&L and change_pct rather than from a stored prior snapshot.

Weights are computed against net liquidation ($60,068.80, cash included). On a positions-only basis ($50,994.96) SPWO is 13.2% and NVO is 10.8% - i.e. the denominator choice changes which tickers breach. Net liquidation was used because the rules set a 7.5-10% cash target, implying cash is part of the allocation base.
Cash is 15.1% of net liquidation, above the 7.5-10% target. This deflates every position weight; at target cash, weights would be roughly 6-9% higher relative.
No 0-share/phantom positions were returned by IBKR this run.
